# Lab 7.7: Cloud Resource Connections

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a connection, read its service account, grant it access, and let another user use the connection.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create a connection.** **Pipelines and connections → Connections → Create connection** (or Explorer **+ Add data → Connections to external data sources**):
   - **Connection type**: Vertex AI remote models, remote functions, BigLake and Spanner (Cloud Resource)
   - **Connection ID**: `lab_conn_ui`
   - **Location**: US

2. **[CLI] Create and inspect one from the CLI.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --connection --connection_type=CLOUD_RESOURCE --location=US lab_conn_cli
bq show --connection $PROJECT_ID.us.lab_conn_cli</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Copy the **serviceAccountId**. BigQuery uses this service account whenever the connection reads files or calls services.

3. **[CLI] Grant the service account what it needs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SA=$(bq show --format=json --connection $PROJECT_ID.us.lab_conn_cli | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['cloudResource']['serviceAccountId'])")
gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://$PROJECT_ID-bq-labs --member=serviceAccount:$SA --role=roles/storage.objectViewer
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=serviceAccount:$SA --role=roles/aiplatform.user --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Share the connection.** Open the connection, click **Share**, and give a colleague **BigQuery Connection User**. They can now use it in queries without seeing any keys.

5. **[CLI] Clean up the extra connections.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq rm --connection $PROJECT_ID.us.lab_conn_ui
bq rm --connection $PROJECT_ID.us.lab_conn_cli</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Keep `us.lab_conn` from Lab 5.8 for later modules.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Connection types | Cloud resource, Cloud SQL, Spanner, AWS, Azure, Spark |
| Identity | Each connection has its own service account |
| Access | Granted to the service account, not to users |
| Sharing | `roles/bigquery.connectionUser` |
